function: Learned multiple-stage booster networks (WUB-Net, OPB-Net, BF-Net) generate IRS phase shifts and receiver beamforming vectors that minimize the maximum secrecy outage probability among users (p. 6, 8)
system: Uplink: BS with Nt=8 antennas, reflecting IRS (unit-modulus phase shifts) with Ns=64 elements, K=4 single-antenna users, Ne=2-antenna eavesdropper; 2 GHz carrier, 20 MHz bandwidth (p. 3, p. 11-12)
method: Unsupervised (label-free) multi-stage booster networks: FC WUB-Net, CNN OPB-Net, FC BF-Net; BF-Net pre-trained then frozen; losses from the secrecy-outage term; Adam, offline training (p. 8-10)
data_channel: Custom MATLAB CSI, 16,500 samples (12,500 train, 2,000 validation, 2,000 test); Rician small-scale fading, log-normal shadowing path loss; no 3GPP or measured data (p. 11)
test_conditions: Same simulated distribution for 12,500 training and 2,000 test samples; sweeps of Ns, Nt, Ne, SNR, coding rate, scale factors; no unseen-condition test stated (p. 11-13)
baselines: Non-learned: without IRS, random phase shift, AO (SDR plus Dinkelbach), AO-Grad. Learned: Single-Loss Net, two unsupervised CNN/FC networks after [22] (p. 11-12)
metrics: Maximum secrecy outage probability among users versus Ns, Nt, Ne, SNR and PLS coding rate Rk; computation time versus Ns (p. 12-13)
complexity: AO: O(IA(KNt^3+K^2Nt^2+ID K ln(1/ε)(KNs)^4.5)+IG K Ns^3) (p. 6); DL: O(Ns^2+Nt K Ns) (p. 11); runtime AO about 100 ms vs DL about 0.5 ms at Ns=64 (p. 13)
openness: Authors' GitHub link (github.com/yiliangliu1990/liugit_pub/tree/master/fairness_irs) cited only for AO-Grad baseline details (p. 12); release of the proposed code or data not stated
q1_support: p. 11: "A log-normal shadowing path loss model is adopted" and small-scale fading "obey Rician distributions"; "all CSI samples were generated using MATLAB". Missing: any 3GPP channel model (3GPP [43] cited only for power control) or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "performance was tested with different values of" Nt, Ns, Ne, SNR and Rk, with one 2,000-sample test set from the same generator. Missing: any statement that a trained model is tested outside its training configuration; layer sizes scale with Ns and Nt (p. 8, 10).
q3_support: p. 11: "The two networks generate phase shift matrix and receiver beamforming vectors, respectively [22]" (Single-Loss Net, learned baseline); p. 13: "instability and poor performance of Single-loss Net scheme" against the MSB schemes in maximum SOP (Figs. 5-9); p. 12 versus non-learned AO: "Both DL schemes, namely MSB-BFNet and MSB-Rayleigh schemes, are slightly worse than the AO scheme".
q4_support: p. 11: "the computational complexity of the DL-based approach is approximated as" O(Ns^2+Nt K Ns); p. 13: "the deep learning algorithm completes its computations in about 0.5 ms" versus about 100 ms for AO at Ns = 64.
q5_support: p. 12: footnote 1, "The details of AO-Grad scheme based on the smoothing technique" can be found at the authors' GitHub link; p. 11: "all CSI samples were generated using MATLAB". Missing: any statement that the code of AO or MSB, or the CSI samples, are released.
notes: Area 3: the learned element sets IRS phase shifts and uplink receive beamforming; the objective is maximum secrecy outage probability, which is not physical-layer authentication. q3: Single-Loss Net follows [22] with a min-over-users loss, taken as an earlier learned method on the same function; AO, random phase and without-IRS are non-learned baselines. q5 borderline: the only link is the authors' repository fairness_irs, cited in footnote 1 (p. 12) for AO-Grad details; the paper does not say the proposed code or data are there, so the reviewer should open the link. Table I and Figs. 4-11 were read as page images (p. 10-13).
